title: I Took the Karaoke Song Limit to the Host Who Booked Encores

parts.text: I took the binder at 9:04 p.m. and the queue tablet already had the host's name six times in a row. The song limit he posted said: TWO SONGS PER TURN. NO BACK-TO-BACK ENCORES. I was thirty-one, Tuesday host covering for a no-show, holding a slip from a shy regular who had waited forty minutes. Jules, the usual host, grabbed the mic. "House examples don't count." I pointed at his sign. He laughed. "Hosts are the catalog." I photographed the tablet, the sign, and the regular's slip. Then I skipped every encore past two and logged a queue-fairness note. At 9:11 the owner asked why Jules's name was on a mic-overage ticket.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The owner can see six host songs against the two-song sign Jules posted.

social.video_title: The host booked six encores on his own limit — Part 1/2
social.description: Shy regular, a queue tablet stuffed with the host, and a two-song sign. I skipped the extras. Would you have passed the mic?

parts.text: Jules called it warming the room until the regular asked for the log. I printed the ticket, the sign, and the photo. The regular sang. Jules sat with a soda and told the bar the limit was always about optics. Optics is a word hosts use when a tablet exists. Queue policy now has a second line: HOSTS ARE NOT THE CATALOG. I keep the binder fair. Jules waits like everyone else. The mic finally sounds like a Tuesday.

social.video_title: Hosts are not the karaoke catalog — Part 2/2
social.description: Queue log, a soda in the booth, and a second line on the sign. Was warming the room ever six songs?
